summary: The principal addition is a separately filed Infectum box. It is independently established by unprefixed ability complement ḥulawwe, k-/g-/ko-prefixed forms and explicit milk/animal objects; the inherited Part act. example already contains finite ko-ḥulwo, so this is a filing gap, not discovery of an unattested form.

Aspect follows morphology: ḥluwaylan with L-agent plus -wa is Preterit-wa, ḥəlwiwayna is Infectum-wa, and gḥəlwi in JTM 2.5/1 remains Infectum despite past procedural German. Temporal me d-/bəṯr məd places completed milking before processing but does not itself settle every weak-final surface form.

Inherited Part act. filing is anchored by agent nominal ḥalawto 'Melkerin' in 94/191. Its embedded finite koḥəlwo does not make that filing wrong; do not move the whole example or add a new nominal box.
Exact source duplicates are withheld: JL 11.12/1, JL 12.14/1, 26/71, 94/191; PrS 35/26 parallels the inherited prs 90/6 quotation. New examples retain edition languages and source spellings.
Confirm weak-final ḥluwənne (JTM 1.1/73): Preterit versus unprefixed Infectum, and object-suffix segmentation in ḥulawwe/koḥəlwənne. Do not normalize the attested forms.
Reconcile inherited prs 90/6 with supplied PrS 35/26 before changing a citation; this may be a numbering-system crosswalk.

The inherited single Preterit example combines prs 90/6 and 94/193 references, but the supplied 94/193 has different processing context. Are these parallel attestations rather than a continuous quotation?

Two argument frames express the same milking event: animal as direct object, or milk as direct object with the animal marked by m-. The same speaker alternates them within one utterance (MAC NE Unfortunate Youth/24); no new sense is needed.
